words.meaning: Friendly and easy to talk to.

words.meaning: Slow, lazy and lacking energy.

words.work: The market was torpid all summer.

words.meaning: To criticise or tell someone off angrily.

words.work: He berated the team in front of the client.
words.gap: The coach ___ the players at half-time.
words.plain: The manager shouted at him for the mistake.

words.meaning: Quick and not thorough.

words.meaning: A natural tendency to do something, often something undesirable.

words.meaning: The idea that every complex system that works evolved from a simple system that worked; complex systems designed from scratch rarely work.

words.work: Gall's law is why we ship a crude version first and grow it.

words.plain: Complicated systems that work usually started as simple systems that worked.

words.meaning: The problem that Scottish, Welsh and Northern Irish MPs can vote on laws affecting only England, while English MPs cannot vote on devolved matters.

words.meaning: The idea that if property rights are clear and bargaining is cheap, parties will negotiate an efficient fix to an externality whoever holds the rights.
